title: Quick check: Bundle Analysis

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Bundle Analysis”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Bundle size should be optimized only after measurement demonstrates a meaningful bottleneck.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Bundle size should be optimized only after measurement demonstrates a meaningful bottleneck.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Bundle Analysis: Bundle size should be optimized only after measurement demonstrates a meaningful bottleneck.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Bundle size?
options: Profile a representative use case before adding memoization or restructuring code.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Profile a representative use case before adding memoization or restructuring code.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Bundle Analysis: Profile a representative use case before adding memoization or restructuring code.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Bundle Analysis” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Bundle Analysis: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
